name: Single-Leg Deadlift
definition: A unilateral unsupported single-leg hinge performed on one working leg, with hip extension as the sole dynamic prime action and the free leg used for balance rather than propulsion. The roster contains five reviewed fixtures: a free barbell, two dumbbell load sides, one kettlebell, and an anchored landmine sleeve. Diamant et al. studied a floor-start barbell single-leg deadlift using an individual eight-repetition-maximum load: the working foot was centered before a standard Olympic bar, the free leg extended behind, the knee bent only enough to preserve the instructed extended back, both hands used a shoulder-width pronated grip, the bar stayed close to the body, the working hip reached full extension, the free foot could touch briefly at the top for stabilization, and the bar returned to the floor. Mo et al. studied continuous dumbbell single-leg Romanian deadlifts with either an ipsilateral or contralateral one-hand load: the dominant working leg maintained an instructed approximately 15-degree knee angle, the bottom trunk posture was about parallel to the ground, and six repetitions were performed at maximal concentric and eccentric speed with an individually matched metronome pace. Mo standardized foot and grip placement but did not report their dimensions or orientation, did not report the free-leg trajectory, and did not separately state whether the dumbbell cycle entered at the top or bottom. Product instructions therefore expose those limits rather than filling them from generic coaching convention, and mirroring either source to the other working side is an explicit catalog adaptation. The fixed 45-pound / 20-kilogram barbell and 25-pound / 12.5-kilogram dumbbell seeds are product initialization, not claims that they equal an athlete's eight-repetition maximum or Mo's flywheel-matched six-repetition load. The sagittal plane classification follows the hip-extension prime; frontal- and transverse-plane control remain stability demands, not invented dynamic actions. Medial hamstrings and gluteus maximus are non-ranked co-primary hip extensors, while the directly measured lumbar extensors oppose the source-described spinal-flexion tendency. Gluteus medius and obliques control the pelvis and trunk. The visible biceps-femoris region remains a stabilizer because its combined mesh cannot distinguish the hip-extending long head from the short head. Surface EMG in the Diamant and Mo protocols supports the distinction of their free-weight fixtures but does not establish numeric muscle contribution, equal activation, hypertrophy, or equipment equivalence. Mooney et al. directly documented a staggered-stance barbell Romanian deadlift but did not report rear-foot load sharing, stance width, knee behavior, grip, range endpoint, bar path, or cadence and combined that exercise with Nordic work and field training. B-stance, kickstand, staggered-stance, flywheel, bodyweight, cable, machine, externally supported, unstable-surface, other kettlebell or landmine load sides, and other familiar single-leg hinge names remain outside this contract. Ulnar wrist extensors and finger extensors receive stabilizer credit as distinct grip-associated wrist/hand-control co-contributors. Krings measured ulnar and radial wrist extensors in deadlift and pull-up categories, but did not measure finger extensors. Forman measured extensor digitorum and wrist-extensor coactivation during grip/wrist-force tasks. Transfer to the reviewed loaded grips is a categorical anatomy-and-mechanics inference, not exact-fixture muscle force, equal recruitment, resisted finger extension, or measured training stimulus. Radial and ulnar wrist flexors are distinct grip-associated wrist-control co-contributors and receive stabilizer roles. Pratt directly measured flexor carpi ulnaris during conventional barbell deadlifts; Mannella measured both wrist flexors during power grip with anticipated radial and ulnar perturbations in a supported, partially constrained robot setup. Transfer to each reviewed deadlift fixture, including the Boxing Science kettlebell and landmine grips, is a categorical anatomy-and-mechanics inference, not direct measurement of its phases or uniformly high recruitment. Forman shows that wrist-flexor activity depends on wrist-force direction and can be low. These roles do not introduce dynamic wrist flexion, equal involvement, or measured adaptation. TFL receives stabilizer credit for unsupported single-leg hip and pelvic control, not hip extension. Collings recorded TFL in related single-leg Romanian tasks but reported modeled gluteal forces, not TFL force or ranking. Transfer to the floor-start barbell, both single-dumbbell load sides, and the Boxing Science fixtures uses unchanged anatomical capability and each fixture geometry; exact TFL phase recruitment, equal effort and adaptation are not established. The Boxing Science kettlebell branch holds one bell on the working-leg side and lowers it just past the knee. Its anchored landmine branch stands side-on and grips the sleeve on the free-leg side while the working leg hinges; neither branch inherits the Mo six-repetition flywheel protocol or Diamant free-bar floor start. The landmine prose repeats lunge instructions, so its photographed hinge and setup define the fixture.

exerciseRules.description: Barbell equipment is limited to Diamant et al.'s five-repetition floor-start single-leg-deadlift fixture.
The Diamant floor-start and brief-top-stabilization topology belongs only to the bilateral-grip barbell fixture.
Dumbbell equipment is limited to Mo et al.'s six-continuous-repetition unilateral-load fixtures.
The Mo continuous maximal-speed topology belongs only to a one-dumbbell ipsilateral or contralateral load.
An ipsilateral shoulder-line load belongs only to the ipsilateral one-dumbbell fixture.
A contralateral shoulder-line load belongs only to the contralateral one-dumbbell fixture.
The one-kettlebell fixture is held on the working-leg side and descends only just past the knee.
The photographed anchored sleeve is held on the free-leg side and logs added plates only.
The anchored arc belongs only to the landmine sleeve with plate-only accounting.
Plate-only accounting cannot leak to free implements.
Free barbell, dumbbell, and kettlebell paths are not anchored and do not use plate-only landmine accounting.
Whole kettlebell mass is reserved for the exact kettlebell hinge.
Whole dumbbell mass is reserved for the Mo dumbbell hinges.
The free two-hand barbell record logs bar and plates, unlike an anchored landmine.

execution.startingPosition: Set a straight Olympic barbell on the floor. Stand barefoot with the working foot centered just in front of the bar. Hinge over that leg, bend its knee only as far as needed to keep your back extended, and extend the unloaded straight leg behind you. Grip the bar with both hands shoulder-width apart and your palms facing back toward your legs; brace your abdomen, tension your lats, and draw your shoulder blades back.
execution.movement: Extend the working hip and straighten your torso under control, keeping the bar as close as possible to the working knee and body while the straight free leg travels toward the standing position.
execution.endpoint: Finish with the working hip fully extended, the free leg almost level with the working leg, the buttocks and abdomen braced, and the lumbar spine neutral. The source allowed the free foot to touch down briefly for stabilization and used a brief top hold.
execution.returnPhase: Lift the free foot again if it touched down, hinge under control, and lower the bar close to your body until the plates return to the floor. Keep the complete timed repetition cycle to four seconds, including the source's approximately two-second pause between repetitions; the publication did not report a separate concentric/eccentric split.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the repetition hip-dominant. Use only the knee bend needed for the instructed straight back; Diamant et al. did not measure a fixed knee or torso angle, and knee extension is not a declared prime action.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the working foot planted and use no belt, straps, bench, wall, or hand support. The source called a torso-parallel bottom posture optimal but did not measure kinematics.
disqualifyingCompensations: Keeping the free foot planted to share the loaded hinge turns the task into a staggered-stance or two-foot-support deadlift.
Bending the working knee deeply to lower and raise the body turns the hip-dominant hinge into a single-leg squat pattern.
Stopping the bar above the floor turns the reviewed floor-start fixture into an unreviewed partial or continuous single-leg hinge.
Holding the bar with one hand turns the two-hand-grip barbell fixture into an unreviewed asymmetric-load variation.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete the set on one working leg, then mirror the setup on the other leg. Diamant et al. warmed up both sides but measured only the right leg; the mirrored prescription is a catalog adaptation.

execution.startingPosition: Choose the working leg and hold one dumbbell in the hand on that same side, aligned below the ipsilateral shoulder. Stand only on the working leg with its knee held at the source's instructed approximately 15-degree flexion. Mo et al. standardized foot and grip placement but did not report their dimensions, grip orientation, footwear, support surface, or free-leg position. The publication also did not separately report whether the dumbbell cycle first entered at the top or bottom; this catalog instruction enters the reported bottom posture with the trunk about parallel to the ground.
execution.movement: Extend the working hip at the source's maximal instructed speed to raise the torso while keeping the dumbbell in the working-side shoulder line and maintaining the prescribed slight knee bend.
execution.endpoint: Reach full working-hip extension without deliberately straightening the knee, rotating the trunk, or using the free foot for support.
execution.returnPhase: Hinge at the source's maximal instructed speed until the trunk is about parallel to the ground, then continue directly into the next repetition without external support. Complete six continuous repetitions. The study used an individual metronome pace matched to each participant's flywheel velocity, not one universal cadence.
execution.controlledJoints: Maintain the instructed approximately 15-degree working-knee flexion and control the spine and pelvis against flexion, side-bending, and rotation. The source did not collect kinematics, so these instructions do not claim literal zero excursion.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the working foot planted and the other foot unloaded, with no wall, bench, hand, or torso support. Do not invent a free-leg trajectory or exact foot and grip placement that Mo et al. did not report.
disqualifyingCompensations: Putting the free foot down to share the load turns the single-leg fixture into a staggered-stance or B-stance hinge.
Moving the dumbbell to the hand opposite the working leg turns this exercise into the contralateral-load fixture.
Bending and straightening the working knee deeply to create the repetition turns the hip-dominant hinge into a single-leg squat pattern.
Stopping well before the reported trunk-parallel bottom turns the reviewed range into an unreviewed partial single-leg hinge.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete the continuous set on one working leg with the dumbbell in the same-side hand, then move the dumbbell and mirror the setup on the other leg. Mo et al. tested only the dominant working leg; the mirrored prescription is a catalog adaptation.

execution.startingPosition: Choose the working leg and hold one dumbbell in the opposite hand, aligned below the contralateral shoulder. Stand only on the working leg with its knee held at the source's instructed approximately 15-degree flexion. Mo et al. standardized foot and grip placement but did not report their dimensions, grip orientation, footwear, support surface, or free-leg position. The publication also did not separately report whether the dumbbell cycle first entered at the top or bottom; this catalog instruction enters the reported bottom posture with the trunk about parallel to the ground.
execution.movement: Extend the working hip at the source's maximal instructed speed to raise the torso while keeping the dumbbell in the opposite-side shoulder line and maintaining the prescribed slight knee bend.
execution.endpoint: Reach full working-hip extension without deliberately straightening the knee, rotating the trunk, or using the free foot for support.
execution.returnPhase: Hinge at the source's maximal instructed speed until the trunk is about parallel to the ground, then continue directly into the next repetition without external support. Complete six continuous repetitions. The study used an individual metronome pace matched to each participant's flywheel velocity, not one universal cadence.
execution.controlledJoints: Maintain the instructed approximately 15-degree working-knee flexion and control the spine and pelvis against flexion, side-bending, and rotation. The source did not collect kinematics, so these instructions do not claim literal zero excursion.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the working foot planted and the other foot unloaded, with no wall, bench, hand, or torso support. Do not invent a free-leg trajectory or exact foot and grip placement that Mo et al. did not report.
disqualifyingCompensations: Putting the free foot down to share the load turns the single-leg fixture into a staggered-stance or B-stance hinge.
Moving the dumbbell to the hand on the working-leg side turns this exercise into the ipsilateral-load fixture.
Bending and straightening the working knee deeply to create the repetition turns the hip-dominant hinge into a single-leg squat pattern.
Stopping well before the reported trunk-parallel bottom turns the reviewed range into an unreviewed partial single-leg hinge.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete the continuous set on one working leg with the dumbbell in the opposite hand, then move the dumbbell and mirror the setup on the other leg. Mo et al. tested only the dominant working leg; the mirrored prescription is a catalog adaptation.

execution.startingPosition: Stand hip-width apart. Choose the working leg and hold one kettlebell in the hand on that same side; log its full weight. Lift the opposite leg.
execution.movement: Keep a slight bend in the working knee, hinge at the hip, and extend the free leg behind while lowering the bell beside the working leg.
execution.endpoint: Lower the kettlebell just past the working knee with the pelvis and trunk controlled.
execution.returnPhase: Extend the working hip to stand tall. The source does not specify whether the free foot touches between repetitions.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the working knee softly bent rather than squatting, with the shoulders set and trunk braced.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the working foot planted and the free leg unloaded throughout the hinge.
disqualifyingCompensations: Putting the free foot down to share load changes the single-leg hinge.
Moving the bell to the opposite hand changes the reviewed load side.
execution.sideOrDirection: Finish one side, then switch the working leg and kettlebell hand.

execution.startingPosition: Secure one end of a bar in a landmine anchor and stand side-on. Hold the loaded sleeve with the hand on the free-leg side; log added plates only, comparing loads on the same bar and anchor setup.
execution.movement: Balance on the opposite working leg with a soft knee, hinge at the hip, and extend the free leg behind as the sleeve follows its anchored arc.
execution.endpoint: Lower the sleeve near the floor without turning the hinge into a split squat or setting the load down.
execution.returnPhase: Extend the working hip and bring the trunk upright while keeping the sleeve in the same hand. The source does not show how the next repetition begins.
execution.controlledJoints: Control the pelvis and trunk during the hinge and let the anchored bar follow its lever arc; the source does not establish an exact grip orientation.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the working foot planted, the free leg unloaded, and the opposite hand free.
disqualifyingCompensations: Placing the free foot down makes this a staggered hinge.
Holding the sleeve with the working-leg-side hand changes the photographed fixture.
Bending deeply at the working knee changes the hip-dominant action.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete one side, then turn around to mirror the setup.
